newsitem.title: USA: Dow surges as Wall Street sighs relief over jobs.
newsitem.headline: Dow surges as Wall Street sighs relief over jobs.

text.p: Wall Street stocks soared on Friday and bonds posted sharp gains after a critical payrolls report soothed the frayed nerves of inflation-wary investors.
The Dow industrials rose 53 points to close unofficially at 5660 and 30-year U.S. Treasury bond rose nearly half a point. The yield on the benchmark long bond dipped to 7.11 percent.

The Labor Department report, a focus of market attention for several weeks, showed U.S. non-farm payrolls rose by 250,000 in the month of August, slightly more than the 244,000 forecast by economists.
The report also showed an unexpectedly sharp decline in the nation's unemployment rate to 5.1 percent from 5.4 percent in July, and a 0.5 percent increase in average hourly wages.
The data suggested that the economy continues to expand at a strong pace, a prospect that has unnerved the bond market of late due to concern that rapid economic growth could trigger inflation.
However, analysts said that the markets took solace in the report's merely mildly surprising strength after a steep sell-off in stocks and bonds on Thursday out of fear of an extremely strong report.
"Yesterday, everybody sold off ahead of the numbers and now today the numbers came in fairly decent," said Hildegard Zagorski, market analyst at Prudential Securities.

Markets had focused almost obsessively on the employment report for several reasons. Economists felt indications of coming inflation would first be felt in upward pressures on wages with labor markets becoming ever tighter.

Analysts had also begun to re-shape their market views to reflect the possibility that the Fed would opt to raise short-term interest rates by as many as 50 basis points at or even before its September 24 policy making meeting.

Ironically, the strength of the report also convinced many analysts and several Fed sources that a Fed tightening was more likely than ever, but as markets had apparently already priced in a steep increase, analysts seized on the bright side of the data.
"We dodged a major bullet," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "At worst we'll see a 25 basis point increase at the September 24 meeting."
"I think the equity markets followed the sigh of relief breathed by the bond market today," he said.

The rally pushed the Dow to a 44 point gain for the holiday-shortened week, its strongest since a month ago, when blue chips added 207 points over five sessions, capped by an 85 point Friday surge sparked by last month's payrolls report.
Financial and transportation stocks, both of which are sensitive to interest rates, rebounded in tandem with Friday's bond market rally.
J.P. Morgan & Co Inc gained 1-3/8 to 88-3/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp jumped 1-3/8 to 75-1/4. Delta Air Lines Inc climbed 1-1/4 to 68-1/8 and United Airlines parent UAL Corp rose 1-3/4 to 46-7/8.

In other individual issues, International Business Machines Corp added 2-1/8 to 115-1/4. Traders cited positive comments by Prudential Securities analyst Don Young about IBM's mainframe upgrade announcement due next week.
Young was not available to comment but his office confirmed that he commented favorably about the new mainframe models, which have been widely anticipated by Wall Street.
Gap Inc gained 1-1/2 to 30-1/2, in a partial rebound from Thursday when investors dumped the shares after the company reported flat August same-store sales.
Several Wall Street analysts upgraded Gap shares on Friday. Lazard Freres analyst Todd Slater called Gap's nearly five point fall Thursday "an over-reaction."
The Nasdaq Composite rose 13.73 to 1139.39.
The S&P 500 index rose 6.24 to 655.68.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
